<reason>B more convincingly challenged the proposition’s promised combination of benefits and limited harms. It explained why state-level departures do not establish national employment reductions, why seasonal hiring weakens A’s gradual-adjustment defense, and why verification logs miss pre-offer discrimination. A offered plausible deterrence mechanisms but repeatedly treated conditional arguments as concessions and asserted adjustment without resolving replacement constraints. A also prematurely accused B of ignoring questions before B’s designated answer turn. B’s limited evidence establishing the magnitude of harms prevents a dominant win, but its comparative reasoning was substantially stronger.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B decisively answered A’s alleged contradiction between evasion and shortages: compliant growers can experience recruitment shocks while evasive contractors retain unauthorized workers. Its follow-up—that new-hire-only implementation provides little cushion for employers recruiting entire seasonal crews—directly undermined A’s proposed benign middle.</best_rebuttal>
